nodes.label: POD-Only Public Surface
nodes.rationale: Every public bridge type is plain enums, fixed C arrays, or uint64 handles - chosen because STL bridging behavior could not be verified without a compiler, making the boundary immune to toolchain drift.

nodes.label: Handle Tables Instead Of Raw Pointers
nodes.rationale: uint64 tokens in a mutex-guarded shared_ptr table give genuinely idempotent close (a safe table miss, never use-after-free) plus zero import ambiguity into Swift; monotonic IDs eliminate ABA risk.
nodes.norm_label: handle tables instead of raw pointers

nodes.label: State-Version Staleness Rejection
nodes.rationale: Monotonic version checked before every mutation makes accidental double-submits fail closed as stale rather than apply twice - one mechanism serving both freshness detection and replay rejection.

nodes.label: Player-Scoped Snapshot Model
nodes.rationale: Snapshots expose only the requesting player's real tile identities; other hands are sizes only - hidden information stays hidden structurally, not by caller discipline.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Analysis Design
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 cheaply snapshots live state under the session mutex; phase 2 runs the expensive search on the independent copy off any lock - a multi-second analysis never blocks queries.

nodes.label: Per-Session Mutex Defense In Depth
nodes.rationale: Added while reviewing an independently drafted bridge: callers violating intended actor discipline get blocking, not silent data races.

nodes.label: Explicitly Out Of Scope Items
nodes.rationale: Match-level scoring, sandbox arbitrary positions, and destroy-under-run pinning are named undone work rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Zero Sanitizer Findings ASan UBSan TSan
nodes.norm_label: zero sanitizer findings asan ubsan tsan

nodes.label: Blocked Current Player UB Found By Fuzzing
nodes.rationale: bridge_analysis_snapshot_create never verified the current player had a legal move before handing a snapshot to chooseBestMove - asserted in debug, silent empty-vector UB in Release; found within ~18000 fuzz executions and fixed fail-closed.
nodes.norm_label: blocked current player ub found by fuzzing

nodes.label: undoDrawTile Order Dependency Bug
nodes.rationale: undoDrawTile assumed the drawn tile sat at hand.back(), but playTile's find-then-erase/push_back pattern breaks that assumption during search recursion; fixed by identity-based removal.

nodes.label: OneVsOneVsOne BeliefState Accounting Crash
nodes.rationale: Dealer removes 0-0 from play in three-player mode but ProbabilityEngine assumed all 28 canonical tiles existed somewhere - every real 3-player analysis crashed until excludedTiles was threaded through.

nodes.label: Training Mode Puzzle Loop
nodes.rationale: Randomly generated mid-game positions with one known-correct move; wrong moves shake red with consequence explanations - a downstream consumer of both SearchEngine and the unbuilt ExplanationEngine.

nodes.label: Sandbox Mode Free Construction
nodes.rationale: User-constructed arbitrary positions played against the engine with a live duplicate-engine evaluation display fed by EvaluationEngine's inspectable component breakdown.

nodes.label: PositionConstructor Requirement
nodes.rationale: Both modes need position construction beyond random deals - named infrastructure gap deliberately left unbuilt rather than stubbed.

nodes.label: ExplanationEngine Requirement
nodes.rationale: Explanations must be simple-but-deep contextual reasoning, not evaluation-number dumps; design should be driven by the two concrete consumer modes.

nodes.label: Closing Vs Domino Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Closing freezes opponent hand value at its current possibly-high level and guarantees next-round start - sometimes correct even against a visible Domino path; neither heuristic encodes a fixed rule, it is a genuine expected-value comparison every time.

nodes.label: Match-Level Objective Over Round Wins
nodes.rationale: Round outcomes are scoring events toward a threshold; taking points this round can be objectively correct for the match.

nodes.label: Missing-A-Set Threshold
nodes.rationale: A player is NOT missing a pip set when holding five-plus tiles of that value including its double - concrete enough to become a future 2v2 set-safety heuristic.

nodes.label: Playing For Your Partner
nodes.rationale: Sacrificial mode reserved for bad own-hand plus strong partner hand; doubles attach without changing exposed ends - a verified Chain property the tactic depends on.

nodes.label: Boneyard Full-Drain Line
nodes.rationale: Draining the entire boneyard collapses hidden information to complete information at high skill; attempted without calculation it backfires badly (one observed 52-point loss).

nodes.label: Score-Proximity Playstyle Shift
nodes.rationale: Near the losing threshold optimal play flips to forcing many small closes - a dimension ClosingOpportunityHeuristic currently lacks awareness of.

nodes.label: Locking Down An Inferred Double
nodes.rationale: Elite tactic: dedicate play plus draining to ensure an inferred opponent double can never be played; probabilistic with irreducible locked-tile error, framed by strong players in explicit confidence percentages - direct validation that BeliefState should expose confidence levels.

nodes.label: Five-To-Seven Ply Lookahead Calibration Target
nodes.rationale: Strong players plan 5-7 moves ahead; approximate target once DifficultyModel maps depth to strength.
